tip.title: WOULD RATHER + SUBJECT → PAST
tip.ruleHtml: Cuando would rather lleva un sujeto distinto, usa past simple para hablar de una preferencia presente o futura.
tip.contrastHtml: No: I'd rather you call / have called · Sí: I'd rather you called.

questions.q: I'd rather you ___ me before making any changes.
questions.rule: Would rather + another subject takes past simple.

questions.q: Only after the meeting ___ the mistake.
questions.rule: Only after at the front triggers inversion; after did, use the base verb.
questions.trigger: ONLY AFTER → DID + SUBJECT + BASE VERB

questions.q: The portal allows customers ___ appointments online.
If Marco ___ the warning, he wouldn't have missed the exit.
questions.rule: Third conditional uses past perfect after if.

questions.q: We'd rather the contractor ___ tomorrow morning.
questions.rule: Would rather + another subject takes past simple.

questions.q: Rarely ___ such a quiet morning in the city.
questions.rule: Rarely at the front triggers inversion.

questions.q: The permit allows residents ___ bicycles in the courtyard.
Breakfast was included, so we ___ food beforehand.
questions.rule: Needn't have means we bought it, but buying it was unnecessary.
questions.trigger: DID IT + NOT NECESSARY → NEEDN'T HAVE

questions.q: I'd rather she ___ the issue privately.
questions.rule: Would rather + another subject takes past simple.

questions.q: Not until the lights went out ___ there was a problem.
questions.rule: Not until at the front triggers inversion; after did, use the base verb.
questions.trigger: NOT UNTIL → DID + SUBJECT + BASE VERB

questions.q: The editor allows writers ___ drafts privately.
If I ___ the backup, I would have restored the files.
questions.rule: Third conditional uses past perfect after if.
Would rather + another subject takes past simple.

questions.q: Seldom ___ this kind of detail on the first visit.
questions.rule: Seldom at the front triggers inversion.

questions.q: The venue supplied headphones, so she ___ hers.
questions.rule: Needn't have means she brought them, but bringing them was unnecessary.
questions.trigger: DID IT + NOT NECESSARY → NEEDN'T HAVE
